- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward pressure, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below prior high or adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat, model overestimates volatility — reduce forecast variance by 10–20% in early horizon (1–7 days) and apply mild downward bias.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often over-optimistically projects continuation — reduce forecast slope by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.
- If recent history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model tends to ignore it — apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecast for next 7–14 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates recovery — reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, especially if recent 18-day average is falling.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.33 for 3+ days), model often fails to account for eventual correction — reduce forecast by 1–3% per 3-day horizon after peak.
